rv.q: Sharrock's loving and beautifully acted revival... mixes anguish, suspense, humour and compassion to often electrifying effect.
Admittedly Anne-Marie Duff is not obvious casting as the happily hedonistic Alma. But she invests the role with a fragile intensity as if she is experiencing a bad dream...
But the play, originally written for radio, has little theatrical dynamism.
After Sharrock’s rapturous rediscovery of Rattigan’s After the Dance last year, this is merely routine.
Thea Sharrock brings splendid tension to her direction of Cause Celebre.

cn.t: Rattigan's final play receives mostly warm reviews in Sharrock's well-acted revival, praised for its emotional depth and gripping courtroom drama, though some find the staging clunky and the production uneven.
